newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.3 pct to fresh record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.3 pct to fresh record.

text.p: The market index at Istanbul's stock exchange edged higher despite profit-taking on Tuesday to reach its fifth consequtive record, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at a new all-time high of 78,711.82, up 232.11 points, or 0.3 percent from Monday's 78,479.71, the previous record.
Trade volume dropped to 19.32 trillion lira ($208 million) from yesterday's 25.79 trillion lira ($278 million) which included a 3.5 trillion lira ($38 million) block deal.

"The market recovered to test the 79,000 barrier again after the morning profit-taking. Activity was led by shares which carried less premiums than others. Shares were being switched," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.
The index which was down 0.17 percent at midday brushed a high of 79,378 in hectic afternoon trade before falling back in profit-taking. It was the second test of the 79,000 resistance after Monday.
Brokers said the market still awaited a major down correction to the continuing medium-term uptrend. The index has surged 21.5 percent since mid-September.
